_note: The 1.0.0 release artifact and the four proofs it rests on. Built in the canonical measurement image from the release tree.
_gating_note: False: this file records an artifact and points at the proofs. It measures nothing itself -- every number it cites lives in the artifact it cites.

artifact.build_tooling: a throwaway virtualenv, so no build tooling entered the pinned measurement environment

the_shipped_closure._note: A fresh virtualenv given nothing but this wheel. This is what `pip install exactdoc` resolves.

1_regression_gate.claim: both lanes PASS at the bound baseline, zero findings. product 16/16 within2pt 0.5274 live 0.9588 dy50 1.045; raw 15/16 0.3615 0.9588 1.6

2_base_wheel_proof.claim: the wheel installs and converts in a virtualenv that never had PyMuPDF: no copyleft package present, 25/25 modules import, 16/16 gated fixtures convert, suite green
2_base_wheel_proof.and: docs/evidence/permissive-shaper-2026-08-06.json shows the two installs produce identical DOCX content on all 16 fixtures, so the `mupdf` extra is not a quality axis

3_live_qualification.claim: live pass 7 against Google Docs: overall_pass true, ZERO blocking findings, 16/16 uploaded and cleaned up, zero orphans, on DOCX verified byte-identical to a PyMuPDF-free install

4_licence_audit.claim: Apache-2.0 with PyMuPDF the sole former blocker, moved to an optional extra; the embedded AFM metrics' provenance is recorded in section 5.4
4_licence_audit.open: section 10 items 1 and 2 -- provenance of the initial source, and legal review -- remain OPEN and were never closable by engineering. 1.0.0 does not claim them.

what_1_0_0_commits_to: The public API: `convert`, `ConversionOptions`, `PRODUCT`, `RAW` and `__version__`. Internals -- the parser seam, inference thresholds, writer profile constants -- are measured values and move when a measurement moves.
what_it_does_not_claim: That long dense multi-column booklets convert well. They inflate their page count badly; it is the headline post-release item and it is stated in the README with numbers.
Platform coverage beyond Linux. pypdfium2 ships per-platform binaries and only Linux is proven end to end.
